title: Foodway
description:
What a dish *means*: whose it is, when it is eaten, and what it marks. The cultural half of food, held apart from the edible half and deliberately **not exported**.

The obvious design gives food its own `dishes/` type. It is wrong by this repository's own precedent -- `place` splits from `point_of_interest` on whether a player can stand there, and `character` from `npc` on whether they speak. A dish is an item whose output happens to be edible, so it lives in `items/` and ships. What does not ship is the flood-bread eaten when the river rises, which is a fact about the Harappans and belongs beside mythology.

culture.description: Whose custom this is, from database/cultures.json. Checked by lint against that file the way `culture` on a character is.

dish.description: The `item_` this is a custom about. The one link across the boundary: the item ships and this does not, which is exactly the split.

occasion.description: When it is eaten. The load-bearing field -- a dish with no occasion is a recipe, and recipes are already a type.

meaning.description: What eating it says. Where a foodway earns its place as a noun rather than a footnote on an item.

places.description: `settlement_`, `place_` or `region_` ids where the custom holds.
